{{Use British English|date=May 2015}}
'''Professor John Leigh Smeathman''' (27 May 1865 – 13 January 1933) was a mathematician and Principal of East London College, England, one of the founding colleges of what is now [[Queen Mary College]], part of [[London University]]. He was also [[Vice Chancellor]] of London University in the 1930s.<ref name ="WWW">{{cite web |url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whowaswho/U210942 |title= HATTON, John Leigh Smeathman |publisher=Who Was Who, A & C Black, 1920–2008; online edn, Oxford University Press, Dec 2007 |accessdate=20 August 2012}}</ref>

==Early life==
Smeathman was born in Street Aston, near [[Rugby, Warwickshire]].<ref name = "Oxford">{{cite journal
 | last = le Beau | first = G. S.
 | date = January 1934
 | doi = 10.1112/jlms/s1-9.1.74
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Journal of the London Mathematical Society
 | pages = 74–76
 | title = John Leigh Smeathman Hatton
 | volume = s1-9}}</ref> on 27 May 1865, the eldest son of Revd J L S Hatton, Rector of [[West Barkwith]], [[Lincolnshire]].

He was educated at [[Hertford College, Oxford]] where he obtained an [[Master of Arts|MA]] graduating with first class honours in 1889 and second class honours in physics a year later.<ref name = "Oxford"/> He also later qualified as a [[barrister]] at [[Lincoln's Inn]].<ref name ="WWW"/> He also studied geometry at Oxford as an undergraduate under [[Savilian Professor of Geometry]] [[James Joseph Sylvester]].

==Career==
He was Director of Evening Classes (1892–1896), later Director of Studies 1896–1908 and Principal, East London College (University of London), now Queen Mary College, 1896–1933. He was Deputy Vice-Chancellor of the University of London from 1930 to 1931 and Vice-Chancellor from 1932 to 1933. He was Dean of the Faculty of Science at the university from 1922 to 1926. He also served as a member of the [[Essex]] and the [[West Ham]] Education Committees during the 1920s.<ref name ="WWW"/>

==Personal life==
In 1897 he married Pauline Carlyle, daughter of R J Henderson of [[Colombo]] and they had two sons.

==Notable publications==
* ''The Principles of Projective Geometry applied to the straight line and conic'', 1913, reprinted BiblioBazaar (18 November 2009) {{ISBN|1117107124}} {{ISBN|978-1117107127}}
* ''The Theory of the Imaginary in Geometry: Together with the Trigonometry of the Imaginary'' (Cambridge Library Collection – Mathematics), 1920, reprinted Cambridge University Press (2 September 2010), {{ISBN|1108013104}} {{ISBN|978-1108013109}}
